seen_animation: Frames 1-3: a line-drawn monkey head and shoulder, facing the viewer, two round ears, brow line, face mask with two eyes and a small U mouth, a spiral tail at right; the head shifts slightly right from 1 to 3. Frame 4: the face mask has slid toward the left edge of the head and the left ear has shrunk, an in-between of a head turn. Frame 5: the head is turned to the viewer's left and tilted down, face mask pressed against the lower-left of the head outline, left ear reduced to a small loop with a tick mark, right ear still full. Frames 6-14: this turned, lowered pose is held with only small shifts of a few pixels; body and tail do not change. Frame 15: the head snaps back to face the viewer, both ears full size again, head raised. Frame 16: same frontal pose, the whole head and body placed slightly further right in the frame.
seen_film: A close-up of a macaque against a pale pink background. Frames 1-3: it faces the camera with head upper-left of center. Frame 4: it begins turning its head to the viewer's left and down. Frames 5-14: it holds that turned pose looking down and to the left, with the head drifting slightly lower and the chin dropping a little more through 9-14. Frame 15: the head lifts and turns back toward the camera. Frame 16: it faces the camera, head now nearer the center-right of the frame.
named_subject: A monkey (head with round ears, face mask and spiral tail), matching the macaque in the film.
evidence: Frames 1-3 frontal in both; frame 4 is a partial turn in both; frames 5-14 hold the head turned to the viewer's left and lowered in both; frame 15 returns to frontal in both; frame 16 frontal with the head shifted right in both. The two large changes in the animation (4 to 5 and 14 to 15) fall on the same intervals where the film itself makes its large changes. No frame shows two copies of a feature. Judged from still frames only; playback was not seen.
primary_gap: Frames 6-14 are nearly identical, so the animation holds dead still where the film keeps the head drifting down and the chin dropping slightly through 9-14.
closes_when: Across frames 6-14 the head outline and face mask move progressively a few pixels lower and the face tilts slightly more downward each frame, so frame 14 is visibly lower than frame 6.
protect: The timing of the turn (start at 4, held 5-14, return at 15), the frontal frames 1-3 and 15-16 that reproduce the doodle almost exactly, the foreshortened far ear in the turned pose, the unchanged body and spiral tail drawn in the doodle's polygonal stroke, and the rightward placement of the head in frame 16.
identity_gap: In the turned frames 5-14 the left edge of the face mask and the end of the brow stroke cross over the head outline and the far ear gains a small crossed tick mark, which the doodle never does; otherwise the drawing is the same as c.png.
